<|channel|>analysis<|message|>We need to find which statement is correct per the paper. Let's parse each.

A. The paper argues that late fusion has certain limitations in spatial alignment. The paper discusses low-level, feature-level, high-level fusion. High-level fusion is object-level fusion. They say high-level fusion depends too heavily on single vehicle sensors and only works when both detect same object; cannot help with undetected objects. They mention spatial alignment: low-level fusion requires aligning point clouds etc. Late fusion: is that high-level? They say high-level fusion is often chosen due to less complexity but not suitable for their needs. "High level fusion is often opted over the other two levels of fusion due to being less complex, but this is not suitable for our needs. Object level relies too heavily on single vehicular sensors and will only work when both vehicles share a reference object in their detection. This does not solve the issue of previously undetected objects, which will remain undetected even after fusion." This addresses issue of late fusion. They mention spatial alignment? The paragraph doesn't explicitly mention spatial alignment but relates to limitation due to needing same detected reference. The statement: "late fusion has certain limitations in spatial alignment" is not exactly what they mention. They don't mention spatial alignment limitation. They mention that high-level fusion cannot detect previously undetected objects. So statement A might be false. They didn't talk about alignment for late fusion.

B. The paper says that low-level fusion is more reliable than feature-level fusion. In the paper, what do they say? They mention categories: low level, feature level, high level. They say which advantages. They said high-level is less complex. They didn't explicitly compare low-level to feature-level reliability. The paper states: "Low level fusion consists of raw data fusion without any pre-processing done to the data. Feature-level fusion takes the features extracted from the raw data before fusion. Finally, high level fusion takes the objects detected from each individual sensors... High level fusion is often opted over the other two levels of fusion due to being less complex, but this is not suitable for our needs." It doesn't say low-level is more reliable. So likely false.

C. LiDAR has advantage of spatial dimension, but disadvantage: cannot accurately perceive license plate number. The paper says: "Native obfuscation of entities or private data such as people’s faces and license plate numbers while preserving the accurate model of the perceived object." Means LiDAR cannot show license plate numbers. So yes, LiDAR can't capture license plate number. The statement: "Although LiDAR has the advantage of spatial dimension, its disadvantage is that it cannot accurately perceive the license plate number." That aligns: They say LiDAR can't capture license plate number clearly. So C is correct.

D. In our experiment, we only used GPS to test the robustness of the perception results. They used GPS and IMU. They mention for robustness testing they skewed GPS readings. But they also used IMU. They said "When integrating GPS and IMU, we observe yields ..." They performed robustness test by skewing GPS. They didn't only use GPS. So false.

Thus statement C correct. So answer \boxed{C}.<|end|><|start|>assistant<|channel|>final<|message|>\boxed{C}
